julia_support: FYI urgent from ACME — embeddings endpoint returning wrong vector length intermittently after autoscale (~13:10 UTC). downstream indexer fails. Sample request+response attached below. Can we triage?

sam_infra: Can you paste the full request headers and the `x-request-id`? Any 401/403 spikes around that time? Token rotation might be involved.

julia_support: x-request-id: `req_0a7f3b9c`, model: `redwood-embed-1024`, sdk: python-embed-0.9.2, retries enabled. Response sometimes has length 1536, usually 1024. curl repro: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1024","input":["apple","banana","cherry"]}'
```

marta_ml: Interesting — 1536 looks like a different model variant (maybe 1536-dim quantized/alternate arch). Under load our smart routing can fallback to compatible variants; if the variant has a different embedding dim we should have rejected it. Can you check the `model_variant` in response metadata?

kai_devex: Also worth checking SDK batcher: older TS/Go batchers split and reassemble batches; there's a past bug where we concatenated partial batched vectors without trimming padding when backfilling. Which SDKs did ACME use concurrently?

julia_support: They use python + ts in different services. Python is on v0.9.2 (pip), TS is 1.3.0. Logs show intermittent 401s right before some bad responses: ```
[13:09:58] WARN auth: rotating token for acct=acme-inc
[13:10:01] ERROR embed-svc: upstream 200 but payload_length=4608 expected=3072 request_id=req_0a7f3b9c
```

sam_infra: That upstream line suggests vector payload size mismatch (3 inputs * 1536 = 4608). Two possible paths: 1) request routed to a 1536-dim model variant, or 2) batcher produced padded vectors and we didn't trim. I'll scope routing logs for `req_0a7f3b9c` and check whether fallback happened. Also confirm whether the `model` param was honored when fallback triggered.

ops_bot: [alert] autoscaler applied burst pool override at 13:09:57 (policy: burst-to-lower-latency-queue).

marta_ml: Quick mitigation: server-side reject rule — if declared model dim != computed vector length then return 5xx with `x-embed-dim-mismatch`. I'll open a hotfix to enforce this and add metric `embed.dim_mismatch.count`. Short-term workaround for ACME: pin to explicit variant using `X-Force-Model: redwood/embed-1024-v1` header or set `model_version` param in SDK.

kai_devex: For SDKs: add pre-send validation asserting len(vector)==model.expected_dim for all batch elements. Also PR to rework batcher reassembly logic to avoid padding leakage. I'll post a repro test. Example python snippet to force single-element batches while we patch: ```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
client.embeddings.create(model='redwood-embed-1024', input=[...], batch_size=1)
```

julia_support: I reproduced locally with a repro script that toggles token rotation and parallelizes two clients; sometimes TS client returns 1536 vectors, py returns 1024 — looks like race between route selection and token refresh. Repro steps in gist: `https://gist.github.com/julia/repro-req-0a7f3b9c`.

sam_infra: Root cause timeline: autoscaler moved some requests to burst pool which only had a 1536-dim variant available. Token rotation happening simultaneously caused a short-lived mismatch where routing allowed fallback variant. Action items: 1) hotfix server-side dim check (marta) 2) backport TS/Go batcher fixes (kai) 3) recommend ACME pin model/version + increase SDK backoff jitter (support) 4) alert on dim_mismatch metric + rollback autoscaler burst policy if counts spike.

marta_ml: PR opened: #4821 (hotfix enforce-dim-check) -> will ship to prod in next 30m behind a feature flag. Also adding reject-with-clear-error so customers get 4xx not silent wrong vectors.

kai_devex: I also have a TS SDK PR for safer reassembly (PR #4825) and a Py backport scheduled. Workaround for now: set `max_concurrency=2` and reduce `batch_size` to avoid cross-batch padding bleeding.

julia_support: Noted. I'll tell ACME to pin model/version and apply client-side batch change. Also asked billing to ignore any malformed calls’ token usage while we sort this.

sam_infra: I rolled autoscaler burst override back at 13:23 UTC. Monitoring dim_mismatch metric now.

julia_support: ACME confirmed temporary fix reduces errors. Will keep thread updated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
